title: Replay refusal-rule changes over 50 past readings before landing
summary: Retry of job 20261028-034820-v3rf, which failed in planning (round 3 of 3) because the plan wrote an unaccepted `<job>/replay.md`. Add an `athena check-reading` subcommand; after checks pass, replay the newest 50 accepted readings through the base and candidate builds, store the result as a typed field the records check accepts, show it to the verifier, and hold the job if more than 10% are newly refused unless its criteria intend a higher rate. Audience: maintainers and the verifier.

defaults_applied.how: Each new behavior has tests; fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test must pass.
Criteria check counts, lists and the hold happening on fixtures.
The check is that a refusal rule is tried on real history before it lands.
Empty history is reported as 'no replay: <reason>', not as a pass.
One focused change with the minimal extra athena-data touch.
The hold is enforced in the run pipeline, not prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Job 20261028-034820-v3rf: its round 3 major finding (replay.md refused by check_record_file's JOB_MARKDOWN list) is fixed by storing the replay as a typed field on an existing verification record, which the records check accepts, with a schema round-trip test; no replay.md is created. If no suitable existing record carries it, a new typed record kind is used instead, with the same test.

Finding on pipeline test override: the #[cfg(test)] override sits in front of tree resolution and the subcommand probe and returns the base/candidate deciders, so fixture repos do not skip the replay.
Finding on no-model-call check: compared by model call counts with and without a candidate rule change, with no skip switch added.
Finding on Records::load: use the same `Records::load(&self.git, &head)` call as run/mod.rs; no open question remains.
Because the user chose a typed record, crates/athena-data is now in scope, which widens the earlier file list; the verifier brief still carries the summary and the list, or `no replay: <reason>`.
The 10% threshold is a code constant. Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) do not change.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new `athena check-reading` subcommand takes a stored request and reading and prints accept or refuse with the reason, using the same acceptance rules as reading.rs; a fixture test shows it (cargo test -p athena-cli).
A test builds a candidate-like rule change over fixture records and shows the newly refused requests (refused by candidate, accepted by base) are listed with the count (cargo test -p athena-core).
A test shows the replay uses only the newest 50 requests that have accepted readings, and that an empty history gives 'no replay: <reason>' and not a pass (cargo test -p athena-core).

A test shows more than 10% newly refused is held with the list, exactly 10% or less is not held, and a candidate whose criteria intend a higher rate is not held, with the replay still recorded (cargo test -p athena-core).

A pipeline test, with the override in front of tree resolution and the subcommand probe, holds a candidate over the threshold (Rejected, not landed); the typed replay record and the Athena Blocker finding name the list, and the records check accepts the job directory; no replay.md is created (cargo test -p athena-core).
A typed replay field or record kind has a schema round-trip test and passes the records check (cargo test -p athena-data).
A pipeline test shows model call counts are equal for a run with a candidate rule change and a run without one, so the replay makes no model call (cargo test -p athena-core).

A test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs shows the verifier brief carries the replay summary (newly refused count, total, list) or `no replay: <reason>`, and stays within its size limit with a very long list (cargo test -p athena-context).
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the subcommand, the replay, the 10% hold, the typed record and the verifier brief summary.
git diff shows no change to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows; the 10% threshold is a code constant; no existing reading rule changed.

out_of_scope: Detecting refusal-rule changes by a flag or by matching diffs
Creating a free-form replay.md in the job directory
Adding a switch to skip the replay
departures: Wider scope than the reference (athena-data schema plus pipeline, CLI and brief changes) raises cost and time and lowers the pass chance; a previous attempt already failed.
urgent_reason: It cuts planning stops: the earlier attempt failed in planning because the plan's record file was refused by the records check, and the refusal-rule incident it prevents stopped three drains.
hard_reason: It adds a gate that can hold a job, changes the run pipeline after checks, and changes the records schema that every job's closing commit is validated against.
